# Overview

Analyzing questions related to funding and constraints.

Research questions:\
- How are OSPOs funded?\
- What fraction of OSPO contributors are volunteers?\
- What are the OSPOs' biggest blockers?\

Relevant survey questions:\
- How are your OSPO activities funded or allocated?\
- Roughly how many people regularly spend time on OSPO activities without being formally resourced?\
- Which of the following blockers has your OSPO encountered?\


# Import packages, utilities, and config variables
```{r}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)

source("utils.R")

# Read config.yml
cfg <- config::get()
```

# Load data
```{r}
org_responses <- read_excel(file.path(cfg$curated_path, "orgs.xlsx"), sheet="responses")
codebook <- read_excel(file.path(cfg$data_path, "codebook.xlsx"))

ospo_funding <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "ospo_funding.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, skip_empty_rows = FALSE)

sata_other <- read_tsv(file.path(cfg$data_path, "sata_other.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, skip_empty_rows = FALSE)
```



# How are OSPOs funded?
First, inspect answers from each org and check for disagreement from within the same org.
```{r}
ospo_funding$organization <- org_responses$organization

dupes <- ospo_funding |>
  group_by(organization) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |> 
  arrange(organization, .by_group = TRUE)

# Keep commented for privacy!!
# dupes
```

As usual, there is some disagreement. Let's consolidate using my go-to heuristic: if anybody from that org said yes, then it's a yes from that org.

```{r}
ospo_funding_consolidated <- consolidate_org_responses_yn(ospo_funding)
```


```{r}
count_yes_responses(ospo_funding_consolidated)
```

On average, how many resourcing sources does each OSPO have?

```{r}
# Convert y/n to 1/0
tmp <- ospo_funding_consolidated |>
  mutate(across(names(ospo_funding_consolidated)[-1], ~ if_else(. == "Yes", 1, 0))) |>
  select(-organization)

# Get mean number of yeses per row (organization)
mean(rowSums(tmp))
```

# What fraction of OSPO contributors are volunteers?

First, inspect answers from each org and check for disagreement from within the same org.
```{r}
mc_simple$organization <- org_responses$organization
volunteers <- mc_simple |>
    select(volunteers, organization)

dupes <- volunteers |>
  group_by(organization) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |> 
  arrange(organization, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  select(volunteers, organization)

# Keep commented for privacy!!
# dupes
```

Okay, great. I can see that only at one university did all respondents give a consistent answer. Similar to what I did in the "tools" notebook, I am going to just take the largest of the answers, because I expect that people are more likely to underestimate than overestimate on this one.

```{r}
# Order of preference: keep whichever is further down the list
ordered_sizes <- c(
    "I don't know",
    "None",
    "1 person",
    "2 to 5 people",
    "6-10 people"
)

volunteers_consolidated <- volunteers |>
  mutate(volunteers = factor(volunteers, levels = ordered_sizes)) |>
  group_by(organization) |>
  slice_max(volunteers, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(volunteers = as.character(volunteers))


volunteers_consolidated |> count(volunteers)
```

# What are the OSPOs' biggest blockers?

This was a matrix question. I'll start by recoding the likert scale responses to numbers.

```{r}
score_map <- c(
  "Not a blocker for us" = 0L,
  "Minor, we work around it" = 1L,
  "Moderate, it slows us down" = 2L,
  "Major, it limits our impact" = 3L
)

# Convert all text columns to numeric values
blockers_numeric <- blockers |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ score_map[.x]))
```

Hmm. I considered consolidating these to per-organization answers, but this feels like a pretty individualized question, so I'm actually not going to worry about multiple answers from the same org. We are just doing a survey of OSPO workers, and some of them happen to be from the same OSPO, but we're not going to consider that a concerning source of variation.

Also, I see that there are quite a few NAs. This can skew our averages. I'm going to report 2 numbers: severity (average of answers) and reach (how many people answered).

```{r}
summary_table <- blockers_numeric |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "challenge",
    values_to = "score"
  ) |>
  group_by(challenge) |>
  summarise(
    responses = sum(!is.na(score)),
    reach_pct = round(mean(!is.na(score)) * 100, 1),
    severity = round(mean(score, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(severity))

print(summary_table)
```

Okay, so most of the questions had a response rate of >90%. That's good. In that case, I don't feel too bad about reporting severity only, as reach doesn't vary much.
